- **What survives a reboot on this host** (`findmnt -no TARGET,FSTYPE -T`, 2026-11-24): `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` = `/run/user/1000` **tmpfs** (the socket dir `viola/` and every endpoint gone at a reboot, and at a logout); `/home` **btrfs** (the home `~/.viola`: `snapshot.json`, `snapshot.json.lock`, `heartbeat`, `events.ndjson`, `diagnostics/` survive); `/tmp` **tmpfs** (test homes behind `target/e2e-home` do not survive). `/proc/stat` `btime` is readable (1795464271 = 2026-11-23T21:04:31Z, `uptime -s` agrees).

- **«Was live before the host went down» vs «ended on purpose»:** the snapshot is never removed at a wrapper's end (no remove in `src/run`, `src/cmd/run.rs`); the heartbeat simply stops; `pump_child` writes `process-exit` only on a child exit (a SIGHUP / SIGTERM to the wrapper, which installs no handler, ends it with no line). After a reboot every wrapper reads `Gone` (pid absent or reused, start time differs). What tells the two apart on disk: (1) the heartbeat mtime against `btime` — a beat older than this boot was alive in an earlier boot; (2) the events log after the newest `session-start`: a `session-end` line, which an explicit `/exit` writes and the hook appends even with the wrapper gone. **Unmeasured, live only:** whether claude 2.1.330 runs its SessionEnd hook on a graceful shutdown (SIGTERM / SIGHUP), which would make a rebooted session read «ended on purpose»; and the SessionEnd `reason` is dropped at the parse (crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:238), so no word tells `/exit` from `logout`.

- **A recorded window after a reboot:** the address is the compositor's and dies with it; `workspace` is a Hyprland workspace id (an i32) that names the same numbered workspace after a restart; `placement` records how the last window step ended (`placed` · `unplaced` · …), not a place. So «its recorded workspace and placement» can mean only: move the new window to the recorded workspace id when one was recorded; a hand-started session has no window record (the snapshot's `window` absent).

- **Parent-before-child order:** from the snapshot's `lineage.parent` (self-reported, authenticates nothing); a parent naming no selected instance makes a root; a cycle is drawn once from its first name (rows.rs:20-24) — `up` can reuse the same order over the selected set.

body:
- (verb) `viola up` takes exactly the gone instances whose heartbeat is older than this boot and whose log holds no
  `session-end` after the newest `session-start`, plus any named instance whose heartbeat is older than this boot;
  skips `already-live` and `stale-heartbeat` ones; leaves out the rest — proven by `up_plan_takes_only_a_beat_older_than_the_boot`,
  `up_plan_leaves_out_an_instance_ended_after_its_last_start`, `up_plan_skips_a_live_or_stale_instance` and
  `up_leaves_out_an_instance_ended_on_purpose_or_this_boot` (entries `-E 'test(/::up_plan_|…/)'` and
  `-E 'test(/^up_/)'`), each guard's control held (founder-forks U1 arm 1, PROVISIONAL).

- (verb) Parents are re-opened before their children, a missing parent a root, a cycle taken once — proven by
  `up_plan_orders_parents_before_children` and `up_reopens_each_pre_boot_instance_parents_first` (the spawn order in
  `foot-spawns.ndjson`), the `up-order` control held.

- (verb) Each re-opened instance runs in a `foot` spawned directly with the closed argv of step 9 and resumes its
  newest logged id in place through revive: its revived start's records from its own offset hold `wheel`, `lineage`,
  `launch`, `window` and a `session-start` of source `resume` with that id (tests ·
  decision/start-lines-read-from-start-offset) — `up_reopens_each_pre_boot_instance_parents_first`.

- (window) A revive under `--origin` moves its own terminal's window to the workspace its snapshot recorded, and
  records it; with no recorded workspace it records `unplaced`; a revive without the flag runs no window step —
  `revive_window_ask_takes_the_recorded_workspace`, `up_moves_each_window_to_its_recorded_workspace`,
  `up_opens_a_hand_started_instance_unplaced` and the `cli_revive` cases (founder-forks U2 arm 1, U3 arm 1,
  PROVISIONAL).

- (output) One line per instance taken or named, its word from the closed set of step 10, ASCII, no SGR; `--json` one
  document of names and closed words; `--dry-run` spawns nothing; a refused board is exit 21 with no line; no address,
  pid or workspace on a line (design · contract/cli-verb-output/focus's rule; obs ·
  decision/strict-modes-refusal-writes-no-line) — the `up_*` output cases and `contract_error_bodies`.

- (state) `up` writes neither `snapshot.json` nor `stamps.json` (tests · decision/single-writer-state-files) —
  `up_writes_neither_snapshot_nor_stamps`.

- (tables) `viola --help`'s `setup:` row reads `open, run, revive, up, verify, plugin install`; `boot-time-unread` is a
  row of the exit-cause table with its own hint; the two new readers are bounded census rows — the readers' entry.
- (tests) every entry of the block above that is not `operator` and not `defer`red reads its expect.

- **matrix#v2-12** (gated: R4, viola up once on a real compositor over a planted fleet (R4a) and once after a real
  reboot over a real parent and child (R4b), at the operator host, unlocked, its moments his to name (founder-forks
  U1-U5)) — after a real host restart, one `viola up` re-opens the parent and child that were live before it, each
  resumed in place on its logged id, in its recorded workspace, parent first, one line each; and over a planted fleet
  on the real compositor each window lands on its recorded workspace. Read only from `evidence/r4.md`'s two green
  lines (the gated entry); the fakes never verify it.
- `inputs#I1` — the directive (scope v2-12, nothing live, the forks' away form, the measurements, the live readings).

- Research files inspected: `src/cmd/revive.rs`, `src/cmd/open.rs`, `src/run/window.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`,
  `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/heartbeat.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs`,
  `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs`, `src/cmd/hook.rs`, `src/human/board/rows.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/foot.rs`.

- Code-graph: `start` · `collision_check` · `checked_exe` · `pump_child` · `preflight` callers at src/cmd/run.rs:280-305,
  src/cmd/revive.rs:159-172, src/cmd/open.rs:91-113 (`tree-query-2026-11-24-viola-up.json`).

- `up` running revive in its own process — rejected: revive's child holds the terminal it runs in (`pump_child`), one
  terminal per instance is the only place a resumed session can live.

- `up` handing the recorded workspace on revive's argv (`--place`) — rejected on U2's conservative arm: it would carry
  the window record onto a child's argv (security-plan · decision/window-record-kept-to-snapshot-and-event-log); the
  wrapper reads its own record instead.

- `up` moving the windows itself through the seam — rejected: only the wrapper's own window step moves a window
  (security-plan · decision/window-step-moves-own-terminal-window), and only it records one.
- An MCP `up` tool — rejected: a further boundary widening (founder-forks U5); the MCP tool set stays five.

- Starting the fleet in parallel — rejected (T2): the automatic-verify lock and the pinned-copy placement favour one
  start at a time, and the stand-in `hyprctl` answers one terminal at a time.

- A new time bound for the fleet — rejected: the two a11y time-bound lists are full and wait on the operator's fork F1
  of run `2026-11-24T00-26-24Z-wrap`; `up` reuses `OPEN_LIVE_BOUND` per instance.

- Reading the SessionEnd `reason` to tell `/exit` from a shutdown — out of scope: it is a Claude payload shape needing
  a capability-ledger row and a verify probe; R4b measures what a graceful shutdown leaves instead.

- Do not write a snapshot, event line or stamp from `up`; do not print a window address, pid or workspace; do not run
  any live phase of `scripts/r4-up.sh` from implement.

- Reuse, do not copy: `classify` / `same_process` (crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs:27, :90), `session_chain`
  (replay.rs:192), `read_snapshot_or_replay`, `board::scan`, `run::agents::read_here`, `run::resolve_program`,
  `checked_exe`, `pin_bytes`, open's spawn and `wait_live` (open.rs:330, :357).

- A candidate's `beat_before` reads the heartbeat file's mtime (heartbeat.rs:21-26); a test ages it the way
  `age_beat` does (tests/cli_revive.rs:91-98), to a time before the host's boot, read in the test from `/proc/stat`.

- The fake `hyprctl` answers `clients` with the window of the last `foot-pid` (src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs:108)
  — sound only because `up` settles one instance before the next spawn (T2); a parallel `up` would break the fakes'
  answer as well as the lock.

- `foot-argv` stays written as today so `tests/cli_open.rs` reads it unchanged; `foot-spawns.ndjson` is the per-spawn
  record (step 13). Sweep `foot_argv|FOOT_ARGV|foot-argv` over `tests src`: 14 hits in 3 files (research §Sweeps).

- R4b's scratch root lies under `target/r4/` on `/home` because `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `/tmp` are tmpfs on this host
  (`findmnt`, research §Measurements): a scratch home there would not outlive the reboot it measures.

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan · decision/open-terminal-direct-spawn — `up`'s terminal starts the pinned
  `viola revive <name> --origin <word>`, a boundary widening on founder-forks U2 arm 1 (pattern `rul-r74hshif` /
  `rul-p2zl2kgl`; delegate overseer, the operator away — the wrap's full escalation, PROVISIONAL).

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan · decision/run-window-flags-checked — its twin for revive's hidden
  `--origin` (the same widening, the same authority).

- Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home and runtime dir, and every test ends the stand-in terminal
